newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat planting slowed by wet weather.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat planting slowed by wet weather.

text.p: Planting of winter wheat in Oklahoma was slowed as more rain fell across all districts during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.

"Many acres of wheat will need to be replanted due to damage caused by the heavy rains," the report said. "Since Sept. 1, all districts are above average on precipitation, except the central district which is only slightly behind."
Wheat planting advanced to 25 percent, slightly ahead of 24 percent last year but sharply lagging the five-year average of 50 percent.
Corn harvested 63 percent vs 53 y/a, 77 average.
Corn mature 77 percent vs 81 y/a, 94 avge.
Corn rated 89 percent good to excellent, 9 fair, 2 poor.
Sorghum harvested 13 percent vs 5 y/a, 9 avge.
Sorghum mature 42 percent vs 16 y/a, 26 avge.
Soybeans harvested 15 percent vs 14 y/a, 16 avge.
Soybeans mature 66 pct vs 36 y/a, 48 avge.
Soybeans rated 72 pct good to excellent, 20 fair, 8 poor to very poor.
Cotton bolls opening 31 percent vs 12 y/a, 45 avge.
Cotton harvested 1 percent vs nil y/a, 3 avge.
Cotton rated 32 pct good to excellent, 47 fair, 21 poor to very poor.
Pasture and range condition was rated 76 pct good to excellent, versus 77 at that level last week.
